queer_characters.name: Sita
queer_characters.notes: The source states the film explicitly portrays her romantic and sexual relationship with Radha; she represents youthful rebellion against traditional constraints. Uses 'queer' umbrella because the text describes a woman-loving-woman relationship but the film/director resisted a fixed 'lesbian' label.
queer_characters.contest_notes: The director rejected the 'lesbian film' framing, calling it about 'the choices we make in life' broadly; critics and activists read it as a lesbian relationship. Sita is also married to a man, leaving her specific identity label open to interpretation.

queer_characters.name: Radha
queer_characters.notes: The source states the film explicitly portrays her romantic and sexual relationship with Sita; she embodies a woman awakening to her own agency and desires. Uses 'queer' umbrella since the text supports a same-sex relationship but not a specific self-applied label.
queer_characters.contest_notes: Director framed the film as about choices and female independence rather than a 'lesbian film,' while reviewers and activists read it through a lesbian-rights lens. Radha is married to a man, so a more specific label is unsupported by the text.
